correctness.rationale: The focal proof supplies the asymptotic, both convergence steps, and the positive conformal factor. Applying its finite-trigonometric-sum lemma to \(-P\) as well as \(P\) gives two-sided recurrent signs. A finite alternating sign pattern survives both convergence passages and forces \(N\) disjoint sign-change zeros. The prescribed set has no real points, so those zeros are extraneous.

value.rationale: The number of extraneous zeros is a natural structural measure of failure of a prescribed-zero extremal problem. Proving unbounded finite multiplicity shows the \(\alpha>1\) failure is qualitatively stronger than a one-zero counterexample and extracts the full finite oscillatory consequence of the focal construction.
